text:
Here are five practice questions, roughly ordered from foundational to applied.

**1.** You are reporting to the board on ISMS effectiveness. Name three metrics you would include in a quarterly security dashboard and explain why each one matters to a non-technical audience.

**2.** Your vulnerability management SLA says critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 7 days. Last quarter, 82% of criticals were closed within SLA. The board asks whether this is good. How do you contextualize that number, and what additional data points would you present alongside it to give a fair picture?

**3.** You track phishing simulation click rates and they have dropped from 18% to 4% over 12 months. A colleague argues this proves the awareness programme is working. What are two reasons the metric alone might be misleading, and what would you measure in addition to validate the conclusion?

**4.** ISO 27001 clause 6.2 requires measurable security objectives. Draft two objectives for your organisation (the mid-sized SaaS fintech from our earlier work) that meet the clause 6.2 requirements: each must state what will be done, what resources are needed, who is responsible, when it will be completed, and how results will be evaluated.

**5.** Your CISO wants a single composite "security score" to present to investors. What are the risks of reducing a security programme to one number, and how would you design a scoring model that remains useful without being misleading? Consider what inputs you would use, how you would weight them, and what caveats you would attach.

Want me to walk through model answers for any of these?
